description: §17.1.1 if/else-if/else chain — ONLY the active branch exists in the DOM. Each branch here carries a ${@label} interpolation, which is the shape that used to force the per-branch display-toggle fallback (`<div data-scrml-chain-branch="K" style="display:none">`): a hidden wrapper EXISTS in the DOM, so it violated §17.1.1's own sentence. @step seeds 1, so #one is present with its interpolation rendered and #two / #rest have count 0. A click advances to step 2 and the presence moves: #two present, #one and #rest count 0 — proving both that the outgoing branch is REMOVED (not re-hidden) and that the incoming branch's interpolation is bound at mount time.
rationale: §17.1.1: "only one span exists in the DOM at any time" — EXISTS, not "is visible". A display-toggled branch exists while hidden, so a chain that hid its non-active branches was non-conformant for the same reason a display-toggled standalone `if=` was (§17.1 / §17.2). Both were decided by one predicate (isCleanIfNode, reached for chains through isCleanChainBranch); pinning the chain here stops the two constructs drifting apart again, which is observable to adopter CSS (`:nth-child`, sibling combinators) and to `.children` counts.
